topic: Peptides your body makes: EPO (erythropoietin), the kidney's thin-air hormone. In adults the kidney makes >90% of EPO, in peritubular fibroblast-like cells (Bussolati et al., JASN 2013); low oxygen lets HIF build up and switch on the EPO gene (Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2019, Kaelin, Ratcliffe, Semenza); EPO is a 165-amino-acid glycoprotein hormone (Jelkmann, Transfus Med Hemother 2013); at high altitude plasma EPO peaks by 48 h then falls to a level still above sea-level values (Vizcardo-Galindo et al., High Alt Med Biol 2020; Mairbaurl, Front Physiol 2018); reticulocytes peak ~7 days, total red cell volume rises after >3 weeks; extra red cells cleared after descent (neocytolysis; polycythemia after 5,260 m reverted within ~1 week) (Mairbaurl 2018)

Your kidneys can sense thin air.

Here's what happens on a trek.

02/07

Up high: less oxygen.

Kidney cells notice the drop.

03/07

EPO

Erythropoietin. 165 amino acids.

Kidneys make over 90% of it.

04/07

Low oxygen builds up a protein: HIF.

HIF turns the EPO gene on.

Nobel Prize, 2019
